mainTopic: Can a מחוסר כפורים of a זב burn the פרה אדומה, and where do we learn that a כהן missing his clothes invalidates the עבודה?
overview: The גמרא explains that רבה's view rests on the idea that a זב who immersed but has not yet brought his קרבן (a מחוסר כפורים) is still considered like a זב. It then suggests this idea is a מחלוקת תנאים, citing a ברייתא where the תנא קמא lets a מחוסר כפורים burn the פרה אדומה and יוסף הבבלי does not. The גמרא rejects that suggestion: everyone agrees he is like a זב. The real argument is about how far the פסוק "וְהִזָּה הַטָּהֹר" goes. The תנא קמא says it covers impurity from anywhere in the תורה. יוסף הבבלי says it covers only the impurity of the פרה section, so lighter cases come in by קל וחומר but the זב, whose impurity comes from his own body, does not. The גמרא then turns to a new topic from the משנה: the source that a כהן missing his priestly clothes invalidates the עבודה. רבי יוחנן learns from a פסוק in שמות that without the clothes there is no כהונה. The גמרא challenges this with a ברייתא that seems to learn the rule from the wine passage in ויקרא, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why רבה holds his view: a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is like a זב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבה's position: a זב who immersed but has not yet brought his offering still has the status of a זב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that a זב who is still missing his atonement offering is considered like a זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why רבה treats this person more strictly than a regular טבול יום. He holds that a זב who has not yet brought his קרבן is still like a full זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב who has immersed has finished most of his purification, but he still needs to bring a קרבן. רבה says that until he brings it, he is treated like a זב. So his leftover impurity is stronger than that of a simple טבול יום who has no offering left to bring.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this is his reasoning)
Someone who immersed but still needs to bring his atonement offering
A man with a discharge that makes him impure
Is considered like / is similar to

phrases.english: He holds that one missing atonement, of a zav,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבה, whose view the גמרא was just asking about.

phrases.english: is considered like a zav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from earlier in the sugya about the basis for רבה's position.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the underlying principle behind the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a זב who has immersed is just like any other טבול יום.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה holds that until he brings his קרבן, he is still treated like a זב.

steps.title: This idea may be a מחלוקת תנאים: a ברייתא about burning the פרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question of whether a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is like a זב is argued by תנאים, and quotes a ברייתא about who may burn the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is like a זב is a dispute of תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: if an אונן or a מחוסר כפורים burned the פרה, it is kosher. יוסף הבבלי says: if an אונן burned it, it is kosher, but if a מחוסר כפורים burned it, it is not kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא claims that רבה's idea is actually argued by earlier תנאים. It brings a ברייתא where the תנא קמא and יוסף הבבלי argue about a מחוסר כפורים burning the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that an אונן may burn the פרה. They argue only about the מחוסר כפורים. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will suggest that their argument is exactly רבה's question.

keyTerms.meaning: It is an argument between תנאים
He burned it (the פרה אדומה)
A mourner on the day a close relative died
Kosher / disqualified

phrases.english: And whether one missing atonement, of a zav, is considered like a zav
is a dispute of Tannaim, as it was taught:
If a mourner or one missing atonement burned it, it is valid.
phrases.notes: "It" here is the פרה אדומה, the red heifer.

phrases.english: Yosef the Babylonian says:
A mourner: it is valid;
one missing atonement: it is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְחוּסַּר כִּפּוּרִים דְּזָב כְּזָב דָּמֵי תַּנָּאֵי הִיא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבה's principle from step 1 and claims it is a known מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is considered like a זב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and יוסף הבבלי about a מחוסר כפורים burning the פרה אדומה

steps.title: Suggesting that the תנאים argue over רבה's principle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that יוסף הבבלי holds a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is like a זב, and the תנא קמא holds he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that they argue about this? One holds that a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is like a זב, and the other holds he is not like a זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how it reads the ברייתא. It ties each side to one view about the מחוסר כפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he is like a זב (יוסף הבבלי), his impurity is too strong, so he cannot burn the פרה. If he is not like a זב (תנא קמא), he is just like a טבול יום, who is allowed to do the פרה work. The words "מאי לאו" show this is only a suggestion, and the גמרא may reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (a suggestion that may be pushed away)
They argue
One master holds

phrases.english: What, is it not that they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: מְחוּסַּר כִּפּוּרִים דְּזָב כְּזָב דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: one master holds one missing atonement, of a zav, is like a zav,
phrases.notes: This first "master" is יוסף הבבלי, who disqualifies him.

phrases.english: and one master holds he is not like a zav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא from step 2 would show a מחלוקת about רבה's principle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument in the ברייתא really about whether a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is like a זב?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer comes in Step 4: no. Everyone agrees he is like a זב. The תנאים argue instead about how far the פסוק "וְהִזָּה הַטָּהֹר" reaches.

steps.title: No: everyone agrees he is like a זב; the argument is about the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone holds he is like a זב. The argument is instead about the פסוק "וְהִזָּה הַטָּהֹר", which teaches that a טבול יום is fit for the פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, everyone agrees he is like a זב. Here they argue about this: it is written "and the pure one shall sprinkle." From this we learn that he could be impure in some way. This teaches that a טבול יום is fit for the פרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the idea that the ברייתא is about רבה's principle. It says the תנאים are really arguing about how to read a פסוק about the פרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "הטהור" means pure enough for the פרה, which shows that a person who is still somewhat impure can do it. That is why a טבול יום is allowed. So the ברייתא can no longer be used as proof of a מחלוקת about רבה's principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
By implication, we learn
Someone who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall
The פרה אדומה (red heifer) process

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the תנאים agree about everything. It only says their argument is not about whether a מחוסר כפורים is like a זב. They still argue, but about something else.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees he is like a zav;
and here they disagree about this, as it is written:
"And the pure one shall sprinkle": by implication, he is impure;

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל טְבוּל יוֹם שֶׁכָּשֵׁר בַּפָּרָה.
phrases.english: it teaches that one who immersed that day is fit for the heifer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא proposed in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the ברייתא argues about רבה's principle. The ברייתא itself stays as it is.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument in the ברייתא can be explained another way, based on how far the פסוק's leniency reaches.

steps.title: How far the פסוק reaches: all impurity or only this section's impurity
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא reads the leniency as covering impurity from anywhere in the תורה. יוסף הבבלי reads it as covering only the impurity discussed in this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds it means impurity from the whole תורה. The other master holds it means only the impurity of this section.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what the two תנאים argue about. Their question is which kinds of leftover impurity the פסוק allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says any kind of impurity in the תורה is included. So even a מחוסר כפורים of a זב, though he is like a זב, may burn the פרה. יוסף הבבלי says only the impurity of this section, impurity from a dead body, is included, so the זב's leftover status is not covered and he is disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity
The entire תורה
This section (of the פסוקים)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove a מחלוקת about רבה's principle. Everyone can agree a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is like a זב. The argument is whether the פסוק allows impurity from the whole תורה (תנא קמא) or only the impurity of the פרה section (יוסף הבבלי).

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: טוּמְאָה דְּכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ,
phrases.english: One master holds: impurity of the entire Torah,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, who allows him to burn the פרה.

phrases.english: and one master holds: impurity of this passage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר טוּמְאָה דְּכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection from step 4 by explaining the new basis of the מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different question (how far the פסוק reaches)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to argue about whether a מחוסר כפורים is like a זב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both can say he is like a זב. They argue over whether the פסוק's leniency covers all impurity in the תורה or only the impurity of this section.

steps.title: Why the light cases are included but the זב is not
steps.stepSummary: According to יוסף הבבלי, an אונן and a טבול יום from a שרץ are allowed through a קל וחומר. A מחוסר כפורים of a זב is not, because his impurity is more severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, an אונן and a טבול יום who was impure from a שרץ are lighter cases, so they are included through a קל וחומר from a טבול יום of a מת. But a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is a more severe case, since his impurity comes out of his own body, so he is not included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining יוסף הבבלי's view. It shows exactly which people may burn the פרה and which may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only allows a טבול יום from a מת, the impurity discussed in that section. Lighter cases, like an אונן or a טבול יום from a שרץ, follow through a קל וחומר. A זב's impurity starts from his own body, which makes it more severe, so the קל וחומר cannot reach him.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day a close relative died, before the burial
A dead creeping creature that makes people impure
A logical argument: if it works in the strict case, it surely works in the lighter case
Impurity that comes out of his own body, not from touching something outside

steps.whatToRemember: For יוסף הבבלי, a מחוסר כפורים of a זב may not burn the פרה. His impurity comes from his own body, so it is too severe for the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: Therefore, a mourner and one who immersed that day
after being impure from a creeping creature, since they are lighter cases,

phrases.aramaic: אָתוּ בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מִטְּבוּל יוֹם דְּמֵת;
phrases.english: are included through a קל וחומר from one who immersed that day after impurity from a dead body;
but a זב who still has not brought his offering, who is a more severe case,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן טוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ; לָא.
phrases.english: since impurity comes out onto him from his own body, is not included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what follows from יוסף הבבלי's narrow reading in Step 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Light impurities are allowed by קל וחומר, but a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is excluded because his impurity comes from his own body.

steps.title: Where do we learn that missing priestly clothes disqualifies the service?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic from the משנה and asks for the source that a כהן without his בגדי כהונה disqualifies the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn that a כהן missing his priestly clothes disqualifies the service?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic and asks for a source. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed a מחוסר בגדים among those whose עבודה is invalid. Now the גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן who is missing some of his required priestly clothes
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: One lacking the priestly clothes, from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic from the משנה, after the פרה אדומה discussion is finished
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a מחוסר בגדים disqualifies the עבודה

steps.title: No clothes, no כהונה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from a פסוק that a כהן has the status of a כהן only when he wears his priestly clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבוה said in the name of רבי יוחנן, and some traced it back to רבי אלעזר בן רבי שמעון: the פסוק says, 'And you shall gird them with sashes, אהרן and his sons, and put hats on them, and they shall have the כהונה as a law forever.' When their clothes are on them, their כהונה is on them. When their clothes are not on them, their כהונה is not on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק. The פסוק links having the כהונה to wearing the clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the clothes and the כהונה next to each other. From this we learn that without the clothes, he has no כהונה at that moment. So his עבודה is like the עבודה of someone who is not a כהן, and it is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The sash or belt worn by the כהנים
The hats worn by the ordinary כהנים
The status of being a כהן
And some traced it back to the name of

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule: a כהן's clothes are part of what makes him a כהן for the עבודה. This is why a missing garment disqualifies the service.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: רבי אבוה said that רבי יוחנן said,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָטוּ בָּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: and some traced it back to the name of רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון,
as the verse says:
"And you shall gird them with sashes, אהרן and his sons,
and put hats on them,
and they shall have the priesthood as a law forever" –
when their clothes are on them, their priesthood is on them;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בִּגְדֵיהֶם עֲלֵיהֶם, אֵין כְּהוּנָּתָם עֲלֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: when their clothes are not on them, their priesthood is not on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From שמות 29:9: without his clothes, a כהן has no כהונה, so his עבודה is invalid.

steps.title: Isn't this learned from the wine פסוק instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the source. A ברייתא seems to learn this rule from somewhere else: the פסוק about a כהן who drank wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we really learn it from here? We learn it from there! As a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that if כהנים who drank wine did the עבודה, they made it invalid? The פסוק says, 'Do not drink wine or strong drink... so that you can tell apart the holy and the ordinary.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needs his פסוק. A ברייתא seems to get this rule from a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא starts with a כהן who drank wine and learns from ויקרא 10 that his עבודה is invalid. As the next line shows, the ברייתא then goes on to ask about a מחוסר בגדים. That suggests the ברייתא learns the clothes rule from the wine source, not from רבי יוחנן's פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it learned from here?
כהנים who drank wine
He made the עבודה invalid
To tell apart the holy and the ordinary

phrases.english: But is it learned from here?!
It is learned from there – as it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִשְׁתוּיֵי יַיִן שֶׁאִם עָבַד חִילֵּל?
phrases.english: From where do we know that those who drank wine, if they did the service, made it invalid?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״יַיִן וְשֵׁכָר אַל תֵּשְׁתְּ וְגוֹ׳,
phrases.english: The verse says: "Do not drink wine or strong drink, etc.,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:9–10. The word וגו׳ means "and so on," skipping the middle of the פסוק.

phrases.english: and to tell apart the holy and the ordinary."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in Step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא already learns the rule for מחוסר בגדים from the wine passage, so a separate פסוק seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks about missing clothes and unwashed hands
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues and asks for the source that a מחוסר בגדים, or a כהן who did not wash his hands and feet, disqualifies the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן missing his clothes, and one who did not wash his hands and feet, from where do we know their service is invalid?
steps.whatsHappening: This is still the ברייתא talking. It asks a question, and its answer comes next, so this line sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after the wine case, the ברייתא asks about a מחוסר בגדים. This shows that the ברייתא is about to give a source different from רבי יוחנן's פסוק, which is the point of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Washing the hands and feet from the כיור before the עבודה
From where do we know?

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not the גמרא asking. It is still the ברייתא, which the גמרא is quoting to support its challenge.

phrases.english: One lacking the clothes, and one who did not wash hands and feet, from where do we know this?
